name: Trust Registration
meta_title: Trust Registration Online | Charitable Trust Deed and Setup
meta_description: Register your charitable trust with a professionally drafted deed, sub registrar formalities, PAN and next step 12A and 80G guidance.
excerpt: Set up your charitable trust with a strong deed, registration before the sub registrar and a clear path to tax exemptions.
intro: A charitable trust is the classic vehicle for philanthropy in India: simple to form, flexible to run and respected by donors. Everything rests on the trust deed, the document that defines your objects, trustees and rules for decades.
Krishna TaxNova drafts your trust deed properly, completes registration before the sub registrar and then walks the trust into 12A, 80G and bank readiness so it can actually receive and use funds.
what: Public charitable trusts are created by a deed executed by the settlor and trustees, registered with the local sub registrar on stamp paper of the applicable value. The deed records the charitable objects, trustee appointment and succession, powers and dissolution terms. After registration, the trust obtains PAN, opens its bank account and applies for income tax registrations to receive exempt donations.
who: Individuals and families formalising charitable work
Founders starting educational, medical or social welfare initiatives
Groups collecting donations who need a legal vehicle
Businesses creating philanthropic arms
benefits: Quick, Economical Setup
Trusts register faster and cheaper than most alternatives.
Flexible Governance
Trustee structure and succession are whatever the deed sensibly provides.
Donation Ready
With 12A and 80G, income is exempt and donors get deductions.
Perpetual Purpose
The trust outlives its founders, carrying the mission forward.
Asset Protection
Trust property is dedicated to the objects, insulated from personal claims.
documents: PAN and Aadhaar of the settlor and all trustees
Photographs of settlor and trustees
Address proof of trustees
Registered office proof: utility bill and NOC from owner
Details of objects and initial trust fund
Two witnesses with ID proof at registration
process: Objects Consultation
Your charitable goals are converted into legally sound objects that also pass 12A scrutiny later.
Deed Drafting
The trust deed is drafted covering trustees, powers, succession and dissolution.
Stamping and Registration
The deed is executed on stamp paper and registered before the sub registrar.
PAN and Bank Account
The trust's PAN is obtained and the bank account opened.
Exemption Path
We proceed to 12A, 80G and Darpan registrations so fundraising can begin.
fees_note: Stamp duty varies by state and trust fund value
why_us: A deed drafted casually blocks 12A approval and haunts every grant application. Ours are drafted with the exemption stage in mind from day one.
faqs: How many trustees does a trust need?
A minimum of two trustees is the practical norm, with no rigid upper limit. The deed should provide for appointment, retirement and succession so the trust never gets stuck.
Can family members be trustees together?
Yes, family run trusts are common and lawful. For public charitable status and exemptions, the objects and application of funds must remain genuinely public and charitable.
Is a registered trust automatically tax exempt?
No. Exemption needs separate 12A registration from the Income Tax Department, and 80G gives donors their deduction. We file both immediately after the trust is formed.
Trust, society or Section 8 company: which should I choose?

Trusts win on speed and simplicity; societies suit member driven bodies; Section 8 companies carry the most institutional credibility for large funding. We recommend based on your funding and governance plans.

name: Society Registration
meta_title: Society Registration Online | Societies Registration Act
meta_description: Register your society with MOA and rules drafting, member documentation and Registrar of Societies filing, plus annual compliance support.
excerpt: Register a member driven society for charitable, cultural or welfare work with rules that keep it functional for decades.
intro: A society is the natural structure for member driven organisations: welfare associations, cultural bodies, educational societies and community groups. Governance is democratic, with a governing body answerable to the general body of members.

Krishna TaxNova drafts your memorandum and rules, organises the member documentation and completes registration with the Registrar of Societies, then keeps the annual list filings and renewals on track.
what: Societies register under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (with state amendments) through a memorandum of association signed by a minimum of seven members and rules governing membership, the governing body, meetings and elections. The Registrar of Societies issues the certificate, and societies file annual lists of their governing body; several states also require periodic renewal.
who: Groups of seven or more founding a charitable or welfare body
Educational and cultural organisations
Residents' welfare and community associations
Sports, literary and scientific bodies
benefits: Democratic Structure
Elected governing bodies keep the organisation accountable to members.
Legal Identity
The society holds property, opens accounts and contracts in its own name.
Grant Eligibility
Registered societies access government schemes and institutional funding.
Tax Exemption Path
With 12A and 80G, income is exempt and donations deductible.
Continuity
Membership changes never interrupt the organisation's existence.
documents: PAN and Aadhaar of all founding members (minimum seven)
Photographs and address proof of members
Registered office proof with NOC
Proposed name and objects of the society
Memorandum and rules signed by members
Affidavits or declarations as per state requirements
process: Structure Consultation
Membership, governing body and election design are settled before drafting.
MOA and Rules Drafting
The memorandum and rules are drafted to fit your objects and state law.
Member Documentation
Signatures, affidavits and KYC of the founding members are compiled.
Registrar Filing
The application is filed and queries answered until the certificate issues.
Post Registration Setup
PAN, bank account and the annual filing calendar are established.
authority: Registrar of Societies of the state
validity: Perpetual; some states require periodic renewal
fees_note: State registration fee; renewal fees where applicable
why_us: Society disputes almost always trace back to vague rules on elections and removal. Ours are drafted so meetings, elections and successions run without litigation.
faqs: Why does a society need seven members?
The Act requires at least seven persons to subscribe to the memorandum. For state level societies, some states ask for members from multiple districts, which we verify for your registration.
How is a society different from a trust?

A society is democratic, run by elected office bearers answerable to members; a trust is controlled by trustees under a deed. Choose a society when broad membership and elections matter to your mission.
What annual compliance does a society have?
Filing the annual list of the governing body with the registrar, maintaining accounts and minutes, and in several states periodic renewal of the registration itself. Our calendar covers all of it.
Can a society run schools or hospitals?
Yes, education and medical relief are classic society objects, subject to the sectoral approvals those activities need. We align the objects clause with your operating plans.

name: 12A and 80G Registration
meta_title: 12A and 80G Registration Online | NGO Tax Exemption
meta_description: Get 12A income exemption and 80G donor deduction registrations for your NGO with properly prepared Form 10A/10AB applications and renewals.
excerpt: The two registrations every serious NGO needs: exempt income under 12A and tax deductible donations under 80G.
intro: Without 12A, your NGO pays tax on its own donations. Without 80G, your donors get no deduction, and serious donors simply give elsewhere. These two registrations are the financial foundation of every functioning non profit.

Krishna TaxNova prepares the applications the way the exemption wing examines them: objects, activities and finances aligned, so approval comes without rounds of adverse queries. We also track the renewals that current law requires.
what: Under the current regime, NGOs obtain provisional registration and then regular registration under section 12A (income exemption) and section 80G (donor deduction) through Forms 10A and 10AB on the income tax portal. Registrations are time bound, typically five years, and renewable. Registered NGOs file annual returns and donation statements (Form 10BD) with donor wise details, issuing certificates in Form 10BE.
who: Newly registered trusts, societies and Section 8 companies
Existing NGOs whose registrations need renewal under the new regime
NGOs whose applications were rejected or queried
Organisations preparing for CSR and institutional funding
benefits: Zero Tax on Charitable Income
12A exempts the NGO's income applied to its objects.
Donor Pull
80G deductions materially increase willingness to donate.
CSR Eligibility Foundation
Corporate CSR routing requires these registrations in place.
Grant Credibility
Institutional funders treat 12A and 80G as baseline hygiene.
Renewal Protection
Time bound registrations tracked so exemptions never lapse.
documents: Registration certificate and deed/MOA of the NGO
PAN of the organisation
Financial statements since inception or for three years
Activity report with photographs and evidence of work
Details of trustees or governing body with KYC
Bank statements of the organisation
Darpan ID where applicable
process: Readiness Review
Objects, books and activity evidence are reviewed against exemption requirements.
Application Preparation
Form 10A or 10AB is prepared with the annexures examiners expect.
Portal Filing
Applications are filed on the income tax portal with digital verification.
Query Handling
Departmental queries are answered with documents and explanations.
Approval and Compliance Setup
Certificates are issued and the 10BD/10BE donation reporting cycle is established.
timeline: 1 to 3 months to approval in usual course
fees_note: No government fee for the applications
why_us: Rejections happen when objects, accounts and activities tell three different stories. We align all three before filing, and we run the 10BD donor reporting that keeps 80G benefits real.
faqs: Can a brand new NGO get 12A and 80G?
Yes, new organisations get provisional registrations valid for three years, converting to regular registration once activities commence. We file both stages at the right times.
Do 12A and 80G expire now?

Yes, under the current regime registrations are time bound, generally five years, and must be renewed in advance. Many older NGOs have lost exemptions by missing this shift, which our calendar prevents.
What is Form 10BD?

The annual donor wise statement of donations received, filed by the NGO, with certificates in Form 10BE issued to donors. Without it, donors cannot claim their 80G deduction, so it is now core NGO compliance.
Does 80G apply to all donations?
Donations in cash above two thousand rupees lose the deduction, and donations in kind do not qualify. We help you design receipt practices that keep donor benefits intact.

name: FCRA Registration
meta_title: FCRA Registration | Receive Foreign Donations Legally
meta_description: FCRA registration and prior permission for NGOs: eligibility, SBI account setup, application and annual FC-4 compliance handled by experts.
excerpt: Receive foreign contributions lawfully with FCRA registration or prior permission, and stay compliant after grant.
intro: Foreign donations without FCRA approval are illegal, full stop. Whether it is a foreign foundation's grant or a diaspora donor's transfer, your NGO needs FCRA registration, or prior permission for a specific project, before a single foreign rupee arrives.

Krishna TaxNova assesses your eligibility honestly, sets up the mandatory SBI New Delhi account, files the application with the supporting record MHA expects and then runs the strict annual compliance that keeps the license alive.
what: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act requires NGOs to hold FCRA registration (generally available after three years of activity and a threshold of spending on objects) or prior permission for a specific donation and donor. Foreign funds flow only into the designated FCRA account at SBI New Delhi Main Branch, with utilisation accounts allowed. Registration lasts five years, with annual FC-4 returns and tight restrictions on transfers and administrative expenses.
who: NGOs with foreign foundations or donors ready to fund them
Organisations three plus years old scaling to international funding
New NGOs with a specific foreign grant (prior permission route)
FCRA holders needing renewal or compliance rescue
benefits: Lawful Foreign Funding
Grants and donations from abroad flow legally and auditable.
Institutional Doors Open
International funders engage only FCRA compliant organisations.
Prior Permission Route
Younger NGOs access specific foreign grants without waiting three years.
Compliance Architecture
Accounts, registers and returns structured to survive MHA scrutiny.
Renewal Continuity
Five year renewals filed early so funding never freezes.
documents: Registration certificate and deed/MOA of the NGO
12A registration and PAN
Activity reports and audited financials for three years
Details of office bearers with Aadhaar and passport where applicable
Darpan ID
For prior permission: donor commitment letter and project details
SBI FCRA account details
process: Eligibility Assessment
Track record, spending thresholds and office bearer checks are verified upfront.
SBI Account Setup
The designated FCRA account at SBI New Delhi Main Branch is opened.
Application Filing
FC-3A (registration) or FC-3B (prior permission) is filed with complete annexures.
MHA Follow Up
Queries and verifications from the ministry are responded to promptly.
Compliance Regime
FC-4 annual returns, utilisation discipline and renewal tracking are established.
timeline: MHA processing commonly takes several months
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), FCRA Wing
fees_note: Government fee applies; administrative expense cap is 20 percent of foreign funds
why_us: FCRA is unforgiving: transfers, expense caps and return deadlines are policed strictly and cancellations are common. We build the compliance system with the registration, not after the first violation.
faqs: Can a new NGO receive a foreign grant?

Through prior permission, yes: a specific amount from a specific donor for a specific project can be approved even without the three year track record. We prepare these applications with the donor's commitment letter.
Why must the account be at SBI New Delhi?

The law mandates the designated FCRA account at SBI New Delhi Main Branch as the single entry point for foreign funds, with utilisation accounts allowed elsewhere. We handle the opening remotely; no Delhi visit is needed.
Can FCRA funds be transferred to other NGOs?
Transfers of foreign contribution to other organisations are now essentially prohibited. Programs must be executed directly, a structural point we plan into grant agreements.
What breaks FCRA registrations most often?
Missed FC-4 returns, exceeding the administrative expense cap and unreported changes in office bearers. Each is preventable with the discipline our compliance calendar enforces.

name: CSR-1 Registration
meta_title: CSR-1 Registration | Receive Corporate CSR Funds
meta_description: Register your NGO in Form CSR-1 with MCA to receive corporate CSR funding, with eligibility checks and complete filing support.
excerpt: Get your NGO onto the MCA's CSR registry so corporate CSR budgets can lawfully fund your programs.
intro: Corporate India spends thousands of crores on CSR every year, but companies can route funds only to implementing agencies registered in Form CSR-1 with the MCA. No CSR number, no corporate funding, however good your work.
Krishna TaxNova verifies your eligibility, fixes gaps like pending 12A or 80G, and files your CSR-1 so your organisation appears in the registry corporates actually search.
what: Form CSR-1 registers implementing agencies with the MCA, generating a unique CSR registration number. Eligible entities include Section 8 companies, registered trusts and societies holding 12A and 80G, with an established track record of three years for most categories. The form is verified by a practising professional and filed on the MCA portal.

Section 8 companies, trusts and societies with 12A and 80G
Corporate foundations executing group CSR
NGOs asked by a corporate partner for their CSR number

Registry Visibility

Faster Partnership Closure
Due diligence shortens when statutory registrations are in order.

Complete Stack Check

why_us: Corporates fund compliance ready partners. We deliver not just the CSR number but the full documentation pack their CSR committees need to say yes.
faqs: Is CSR-1 enough to get corporate funding?
It is the legal gateway, not the pitch. Companies still evaluate programs and governance, but without CSR-1 the conversation cannot even begin lawfully.
Does my NGO need three years of history?
Trusts and societies generally need an established track record for CSR eligibility, while entities established by companies themselves have separate routes. We map your case to the exact rule.
Can CSR funds pay NGO salaries?
Program linked personnel costs form part of project budgets; general administrative overheads are constrained on the company's side. We structure budgets that satisfy CSR rules.
What reporting follows CSR funding?
Utilisation certificates, impact reporting per the company's obligations and books that trace CSR funds distinctly. Our accounting team sets this up with the first grant.

name: NGO Darpan Registration
meta_title: NGO Darpan Registration | NITI Aayog Unique ID for NGOs
meta_description: Get your NGO's Darpan ID from NITI Aayog, required for government grants, FCRA and CSR processes. Complete profile setup and PAN linking.
excerpt: The NITI Aayog Darpan ID your NGO needs for government grants, FCRA and credibility, set up correctly.
intro: The Darpan ID is your NGO's identity with the government: grant applications, FCRA filings and many CSR due diligence processes ask for it. Registration is free but the portal's PAN validation and member KYC requirements trip up many organisations.
Krishna TaxNova completes your Darpan registration with a clean, complete profile: PAN linked, office bearers verified and sector details entered the way grant screeners expect to find them.
what: NGO Darpan is the NITI Aayog portal that assigns a unique ID to voluntary organisations, validating the entity's PAN and the PAN and Aadhaar of key office bearers. The profile records registration details, sectors of work, geographic coverage and funding sources, and syncs with FCRA and grant systems across ministries.
who: NGOs applying for central or state government grants
Organisations starting FCRA registration, where Darpan is required
NGOs undergoing corporate CSR due diligence
New non profits building their statutory identity stack
benefits: Government Grant Access
Ministry grant portals require a valid Darpan ID to apply.
FCRA Prerequisite

Verified Credibility

Single Government Identity
One ID recognised across ministries and schemes.
Free and Permanent
No fee, with the profile maintained through simple updates.

why_us: Darpan rejections come from PAN mismatches and incomplete office bearer data. We validate everything before submission, so the ID generates without cycles of correction.
faqs: Is Darpan registration mandatory for all NGOs?
It is mandatory wherever government money is involved: grants, FCRA and many scheme empanelments. Even otherwise, funders increasingly treat it as basic hygiene.
Whose KYC is needed for registration?
The organisation's PAN plus PAN and Aadhaar of key office bearers, typically at least three. Mismatched name spellings between documents are the usual blocker, which we fix first.
Does the Darpan ID expire?
No expiry, but profiles must be kept current, especially office bearer changes, since FCRA and grant systems read this data live.
We changed our board. Does Darpan matter?
Yes, update it promptly. Stale office bearer data creates mismatches in FCRA and grant validations exactly when you need them to work.
